compileNote: Why some compile records are what they are. On the Windows host a translation unit containing nothing compiles in about 30 ms, so the smallest units' wall time is mostly the compiler starting: their preprocessed line count is what guards them, and a recorded time below that floor is not a baseline. Above them, the standard library is most of every unit: on the Windows host the 23 public headers that reach no container or string header self-compile to under 20,000 preprocessed lines and every other one to at least 61,000. The two hosts' standard libraries differ - CoreCheckedSize.cpp preprocesses to 63,520 lines on the Windows host and 11,782 on the Linux host from the same source - so a line count, like a time, is read only against the same host's record. EngineContext.cpp and TaskScheduler.cpp are the only units that include oneTBB's task_arena.h, through runtime/OperationArena.h: an operation's arena is held by its grant rather than by the engine context's state, so that ExecutionContext.cpp and the other units that reach the state do not carry it, and a further unit that needs the arena reaches it through an opaque pointer rather than the header.
includesNote: Why the include ceilings are where they are. A count is a transitive closure, so a header that composes a lower layer inherits that layer's closure whole, and the composition roots of a subsystem land highest. The 44 sibling headers per public header is what Algorithms/Stacking/StackExecutor.h and StackSourceRules.h reach: the executor composes every operation a stack runs - its source, with calibration and both normalizations behind it, the working set, accumulation, weighting and the quality summaries - and StackSourceRules.h states what the source path derives from the whole stack model; 44 of 284 public headers still refuses a header that reaches most of the surface. The 14 standard headers per public header is the twelve the result and image models bring to nearly every operation header - <bit>, <cstddef>, <cstdint>, <exception>, <limits>, <memory>, <optional>, <span>, <string>, <type_traits>, <utility> and <vector>, which Image/ImageStorage.h reaches exactly - plus <array> and <string_view>, which six headers reach together: Algorithms/Photometry/PhotometricColorCalibration.h, the spectrophotometric calibration, fit, samples and transition headers, and IO/ProcessingStateCards.h. Both ceilings bind: a header that would pass one forward-declares what it only names, or splits what its callers need from a composition they do not, before a ceiling moves. The surface as a whole reaches 17 distinct standard headers against its ceiling of 25, and no public header reaches an external one, because a public header that needed an external include root would carry a library to every caller.

isa.note: Object size and compile time for the translation units that compile the same kernels once per instruction set. SimdKernelTables.cpp owns the shared optimized layout, pointwise and reduction families; calibration, global normalization, local normalization, PSF fitting, stack accumulation, the stack column combinations and each compiled demosaic estimate have attributable units of their own. Two variants are measured of each. "floor" restricts the abstraction to the packaged AVX2 rung; "ladder" is what the engine builds, which is that rung plus the Skylake-server AVX-512 subset on the compilers that have it. The difference between them is what one more compiled instruction set costs, which `measure` reports beside each variant.

note: Include, compile-time and object-size budgets of AfterNightEngine, measured and checked by build/scripts/tools/check_budgets.py. `includes` holds three ceilings and the measurement they are checked against: for each public header, how many other public headers (its siblings) and standard headers it reaches, transitively, read from the include directives rather than from a compiler, so the counts are exact and the same on every host; no public header may reach a header that is neither. `compile` holds, per host, every public self-compile unit and every implementation unit: the fastest of several compilations, because noise only ever adds time, and the unit's preprocessed line count, which moves when a header gets heavier and not when the machine is busy; its `isaUnitFlags` are the flags the per-instruction-set units need outside the build. `isa` holds, per host, the object size and compile time of each unit that compiles kernels once per instruction set, at shipping optimization and once per declared subset. A host's records are filed under the id given with --host-id, with the compiler that produced them, and are compared only with a measurement on that host, because a time, a line count - which counts the host's standard library - and an object size all depend on the machine and the toolchain; recording refuses to mix two compilers in one host's records. `check` fails a public header past a ceiling and, given --host-id, a unit or variant the host has no record of and a measurement past its allowance: 1.75x for wall time, 1.25x for preprocessed lines - tighter, because a line count does not vary from run to run - and 1.20x for object size. Without a compiler it fails unless --includes-only asks for the include budgets alone, and without --host-id it measures but compares nothing. A record changes in one of three ways. `measure --record --host-id <id>` adds what the host has no record of and keeps every existing record; it is run after `check` has passed, so an addition joins a baseline that was verified rather than absorbing a regression. A growth that is the intended cost of a change is advanced by hand for that unit alone, once compiling the unit without the change, with the check's own command and flags, has shown the growth is the change's; a number that stayed inside its allowance keeps its record. `measure --record --rebaseline` replaces a host's records wholesale, for a new compiler or a new machine. Every `--record` also rewrites the include measurement, which check_budgets_test.py holds to the tree. A ceiling is raised only when a measured header needs it, for the reason includesNote states; compileNote says why some compile records are what they are.
